questions.text: What does start_session(user_id) do in detail, and what is the sid cookie? You say it deletes the old sid row; whose old row, and what if the browser has no session yet?
questions.about: SESS: start_session user_id, same as password login

questions.text: Where is the next value checked as a safe relative path, and what happens if it is missing or fails the check? Where does it travel between start and the final redirect?
questions.about: GET /auth/google/start?next=<path> / Redirect to next if relative path, else /home

questions.text: In the new-user branch, what values does the INSERT into users set besides password_hash NULL and email_verified_at (for example, name or other required columns)? Where do they come from, since only sub and email are read?
How does a Google-created user with no password end up able to use the site later? Can they only use Google, and how does the 'password reset email' fit in?
questions.about: Users with no password / Unlink: Refuse: set a password first

questions.text: On the confirm page, how does the server know which user and sub are being linked? Is it only the oidc_pending cookie, and is a logged-in session needed or ignored?
The matched user's email must equal Google's verified email. Can the user be matched while the existing user's own email is not verified? Why is the password required then?
questions.about: MATCH: users.email equals Google email? / PEND

questions.text: What does the Error page look like to the user, and where can they go from it? Is it the same page for Redis down, bad state and wrong session in link mode?
questions.about: ERRPAGE: Error page: this sign-in link is invalid or expired

questions.text: After a successful confirmation or login, which cookies get cleared? oidc_state is mentioned as cleared in SESS but also in the callback; what clears oidc_state in the Back and Refuse outcomes?

answers.text: Per auth_flow.md, start_session deletes the sessions row named by the sid cookie the browser sent (the browser's own old session), if any; with no cookie it skips that. It then inserts a new sessions row, sets the sid cookie (value is sessions.id) and redirects to next if a relative path, else /home. Added to a new Terms section.

next is checked once at start as a relative path on our site and dropped if missing or invalid. It travels in the Redis state record, then the pending record, then into start_session, which re-checks it (existing behaviour) and falls back to /home. Added to Terms and to the start node.

Per schema.sql, users has no other required columns. The INSERT sets email (lowercased Google email), email_verified_at now and password_hash NULL; failed_logins, locked_until and created_at use defaults. Nothing else is needed from Google. Added to the state section.

They sign in with Google only until they use the existing password reset email (POST /forgot), which sets password_hash and works on a NULL hash per auth_flow.md. Once they have a password they can unlink. A password login attempt before then fails like a wrong password. Added to Terms and the no-password bullet.
Only the oidc_pending cookie and its Redis record give the sub and matched user_id. Any current sid session is ignored; start_session replaces it on success. Added as a rule and to the POST node.

Yes, the matched user's own email may be unverified in our table. Google's verified email alone does not prove the person controls that existing account (someone else may have registered it), so the account's password is the proof, as the brief requires. Added as a clause. Whether linking should also mark email_verified_at is not decided; it is listed as an open question.

It is one plain page for Redis down at start, bad state and wrong session in link mode, with a message that the link is invalid or expired or sign-in is unavailable, and a link to /login. The exact wording and design are not specified by the brief. Added as a rule.

oidc_state is cleared once, at the start of the callback, on every outcome; I removed the redundant clear from SESS. Since the callback is the only place it is read, Back and Refuse outcomes after that are already covered. oidc_pending is only cleared together with the pending record; refusals before the pending step never set it. Added a Cookies rule.

questions.text: The routes table says unlink 'needs a password', but the flowchart only checks that password_hash is not NULL. Does the user have to type their password to unlink, or only have one set?
What does the user see after a successful unlink, and does unlink also need a session and the CSRF token like the link button?
questions.about: UD: DELETE user_google_accounts row for this user

answers.text: The user does not type their password to unlink. The brief says users may unlink only if they have a password, which I read as a check that password_hash is not NULL, so they still have a way in afterwards. The routes table wording 'needs a password' was ambiguous; it now says the account must have a password set and that the user does not type it, and an Unlink rule says the same.

After a successful unlink the user returns to Account Settings with 'Google unlinked'; a refusal also returns to Settings with the reset-email message. Unlink needs a session and the CSRF token, like the link button, because it is a state-changing POST from Settings. The brief does not specify the wording or CSRF; I chose this to match the link button. Added to the routes table, the flowchart and the failure table.

teachbacks.text:
Walkthrough: a brand-new person clicks "Sign in with Google" on the login page, followed to the end. Side branches are noted where the document gives them.

1. Start. The user clicks "Sign in with Google" on the login page. This is GET /auth/google/start?next=<path>. The server sets mode=login. It keeps `next` only if it is a relative path on our site and drops it otherwise.

2. Making the attempt. The server makes three random values: `state`, `nonce` and `code_verifier`. It also deletes any old pending record and `oidc_pending` cookie for this browser. It then writes Redis key goauth:state:<state> with `code_verifier`, `nonce`, `mode`, `next` (plus `user_id` in link mode). The key expires after 600 seconds. It sets the cookie `oidc_state` (HttpOnly, Secure, Lax, path /auth/google, 600 seconds) holding the `state`. Finally it redirects the browser to Google using the code flow with PKCE S256, `state`, `nonce` and scope "openid email profile". If the Redis write fails, the user sees the single error page ("invalid or expired, or unavailable", with a link to /login). Nothing is created.

3. At Google. The user signs in or presses Cancel. Google redirects the browser to GET /auth/google/callback. A successful redirect carries a one-time `code` and the `state`. A cancel carries an `error` parameter.

4. Callback, state check. The callback first clears the `oidc_state` cookie, on every outcome. It then runs an atomic GETDEL on goauth:state:<state>. The check passes only if a record was found AND the `oidc_state` cookie equals the `state` parameter. If the state is unknown, expired, already used or from a different browser, the user gets the error page and nothing changes. Because GETDEL consumes the record, a replay fails.

5. Google error. If Google sent an `error` parameter, the user goes back to the start page with a neutral "Google sign-in was not completed" message. For login that is /login with `next` kept. For link it is /settings. No state is left behind.

6. Token exchange. The server swaps the `code` for an ID token at Google's token endpoint, sending `code_verifier`. There is a 5 second timeout and no retry. It validates the ID token's signature (against Google's JWKS), `iss`, `aud`, `exp` and `nonce` (which must equal the stored one). If the exchange or validation fails, the user goes back to the start page with "Google sign-in did not work, try again or use email and password". The reason is logged and nothing changes. The state was already consumed, so the user must start over. On success the server reads `sub`, `email` (lowercased) and `email_verified`, then discards the tokens. Only these three values are used. No tokens are stored.

7. Branch on mode. For mode=login, the flow continues as below. Mode=link is described at step 12.

8. Known Google account. The server looks up `sub` in user_google_accounts. If it is found, the user signs in directly (step 11). This is not blocked by `locked_until`.

9. Unknown `sub`, new user. If `email_verified` is false, the server refuses and sends the user back to /login with "use email and password". Nothing is created. If it is true, the server checks whether users.email equals the Google email.
   - No match: in one transaction the server inserts a user (lowercased email, NULL password_hash, email_verified_at=now, other columns default) and inserts the user_google_accounts row. If the email unique constraint fails because of a race, the match check runs again. If a `sub` or `user_id` unique constraint fails, the result is a refusal as "already linked". Success goes to step 11.
   - Match: if that user already has a different Google account linked, the server refuses with "linked to a different Google account" and changes nothing. Otherwise it goes to step 10.

10. Password confirmation for an existing account.
   - The server cannot trust that the Google email proves ownership of the existing account. So it writes Redis goauth:pending:<token> (`sub`, matched `user_id`, `next`, 600 seconds) and sets the cookie `oidc_pending` (the token, Lax, 600 seconds). It redirects to /auth/google/confirm.
   - The page asks for that account's password. On POST, the `sub` and `user_id` come only from the pending record, and any current `sid` session is ignored.
   - If the cookie is missing or the key is gone, the user goes to /login with "confirmation expired" and the cookie is cleared. Nothing is linked.
   - If `locked_until` is in the future, the pending record and cookie are deleted and the user goes to /login with "Account temporarily locked".
   - If the bcrypt password is wrong, `failed_logins` goes up by 1. At 5, `locked_until` becomes now plus 15 minutes and `failed_logins` resets to 0. If the account is now locked, the pending record and cookie are deleted and the link is discarded. If not, the form is shown again. The pending record stays so the user can retry within the 10 minutes.
   - If the password is correct, `failed_logins` is set to 0. A transaction inserts the user_google_accounts row. On a unique violation, the pending record and cookie are deleted and the user gets an "already linked" refusal. Otherwise the pending record and cookie are deleted and the flow goes to step 11. The user's email_verified_at is left unchanged.

11. Session. The server calls the existing start_session(user_id), the same as password login. It deletes the sessions row named by the browser's `sid` cookie, if any. It inserts a new sessions row and sets the `sid` cookie (HttpOnly, Secure, Lax, value is sessions.id). It redirects to `next` if that is a relative path on our site, otherwise to /home.

12. Link mode (side flow). A signed-in user presses "Link Google" (POST /settings/google/link, which needs a session and the CSRF token). If they already have a Google account linked, Settings says "already linked" and nothing changes. Otherwise the flow goes through steps 2 to 6 with mode=link and `user_id` stored. At the callback, the current session must exist and its user must equal the stored `user_id`, or the user gets the error page. Then:
   - If the `sub` is linked to someone else, Settings refuses.
   - If the `sub` is linked to this user, Settings says "already linked".
   - If this user has a different Google account, Settings refuses and says to unlink first.
   - Otherwise the server inserts the user_google_accounts row. No password is asked, the emails need not match, and no new session is started. A unique violation is treated like "linked to someone else". Success shows "Google linked".

13. Unlink (side flow). POST /settings/google/unlink needs a session and the CSRF token. If password_hash is NULL, Settings refuses and says to set a password first using the password reset email. Otherwise the server deletes this user's user_google_accounts row, leaves the session alone, and shows "Google unlinked". No password is typed.

14. Related state facts. A Google-created user has no password and signs in only with Google, until they use the reset email. That email sets the password, marks the email verified and deletes all their sessions. It does not remove the Google link. POST /login treats a NULL password_hash as a wrong password, with the same generic message, and it counts toward lockout. Deleting a user cascades to the link row.
gaps: Who or what clears the leftover pending record and cookie when the user abandons the confirm page, apart from the TTL? Only 'a new Google attempt in the same browser' is named, so this is mostly covered. What the confirm POST needs for CSRF protection is not stated.

How the confirm page's POST finds the pending record: the cookie `oidc_pending` is implied to carry the token, but the document does not say how the GET form is rendered or whether `next` is revalidated there (only that start_session checks it again).

What the user sees on 'already linked' refusals in login mode, and which page they land on. The document says 'Refuse' without a destination or exact message for R3, the unique-violation case and the 'sub or user_id unique constraint' case.

What happens when POST /login is submitted for a user with NULL password_hash beyond 'wrong password'. This is explained. But which `sessions` columns, such as expiry, start_session fills in is not given (not needed for the main flow).

What happens to the `sid` cookie and session if Redis fails after the start step (for example if the pending write fails in step 10). Only 'flushed mid-flow' and 'down at start' are covered. Whether a Redis failure during GETDEL or the pending SET shows the error page is not stated.
Where the CSRF token comes from and how it is checked is not described, only that it is required on the Settings POSTs.
The document does not say what a callback with a missing `code` and no `error` parameter does, or whether `state` or `code` is validated beyond the GETDEL and cookie check.

Open questions the document itself leaves unresolved: whether linked users should bypass `locked_until` (assumed yes, needs the security owner's confirmation) and whether `email_verified_at` should stay unchanged for linked existing users.
